title.narrative: Community Participation for Action in the Social Sector (COMPASS)

description.narrative: The COMPASS Project was launched in 2004 to expand participation, ownership and use of healthcare and education sector services to the community level in four states (Bauchi, Lagos, Kano and Nasarawa) and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) of Nigeria over a period of five years.

title.narrative: Enabling HIV/AIDS, TB and Social Sector Environment (ENHANSE)

description.narrative: Active from 2004 to 2009, the Enabling HIV/AIDS, TB and Social Sector Environment (ENHANSE) project worked with religious leaders and faith-based organizations in northern Nigeria to raise awareness of issues involving HIV/AIDS, reproductive health, and safe motherhood. This organization was one of the first to gain acceptance in this Muslim-dominated area. ENHANSE trained imams on ways to incorporate health-related information in their sermons and community outreach, and also worked to sensitize religious leaders on topics of reproductive health. Lastly, the ENHANSE program provided community leaders with the knowledge and support to influence public opinion and government policy.

title.narrative: Consortium for Elections and Political Process Strengthening, CEPPS

description.narrative: The purpose of the Consortium for Elections and Political Process Strengthening (CEPPS) Cooperative Agreements is to strengthen and support democratic electoral and political processes by providing access to a full array of activities in the field of elections and political processes. The emphasis is on long-term planning and sustainable development of electoral and political processes rather than event-driven, crisis orientated activities centered on a single election.

title.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Palliative Care: Basic Health Care and Support - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

description.narrative: PEPFAR: HIV/AIDS - Basic health care and support, which includes: all clinic-based and home/community-based activities for HIV-infected adults, children, and their families that are aimed at optimizing the quality of life for HIV-infected clients and their families throughout the continuum of illness by the means of symptom diagnosis and relief, psychological and spiritual support, clinical monitoring, related laboratory services and management of opportunistic infections (excluding TB) and other HIV/AIDS-related complications (including pharmaceuticals), and culturally-appropriate end-of-life care. Basic health care and support also includes clinic-based and home/community-based support, social and material support such as nutrition support, legal aid, and housing, and training and support of caregivers. Clinic-based and home/community-based care and support activities for HIV-positive children within programs for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS would fall under sub-element 1.1.8 (Orphans and Vulnerable Children). ARV treatment should be coded under sub-element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and sub-element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services). - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

title.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Orphans and Vulnerable Children - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

description.narrative: PEPFAR: HIV/AIDS - Improve the lives of orphans and other vulnerable children and families affected by HIV/AIDS. Strengthen communities to meet the needs of orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, supporting community-based responses, helping children and adolescents to meet their own needs, creating a supportive social and policy environment. Activities could include training caregivers, increasing access to education, economic support, targeted food and nutrition support, and legal aid. Institutional responses would also be included. ARV treatment of children is excluded from this category and should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and Sub-Element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services). Palliative care, including basic health care and support and TB/HIV prevention, management and treatment, as well as their related laboratory services and pharmaceuticals, when delivered within programs for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, should be coded under this aspect. Other health care associated with the continuum of HIV/AIDS illness, including HIV/TB services, when delivered outside a program for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS, should be coded under Sub-Element 1.1.6 (Basic Health Care and Support) or Sub-Element 1.1.7 (TB/HIV). - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

title.narrative: Media Freedom and Freedom of Information

description.narrative: Strengthen the legal, regulatory, institutional, and information environment which protects and enables the growth in associational life and the development of independent and sustainable civil society organizations (CSOs). Build the capacity of civil society organizations to act as agents for reform and support their participation in democratic decision-making through articulating and representing their members interests, engaging in service delivery, and advocating for issues which become part of the public agenda and are reflected in public policies. Encourage the strengthening of a civic culture which supports democratic institutions and processes, active participation in political and civic life, and the civic virtues of tolerance, pluralism, compromise, trust, and respect for individual rights, including gender equality.

title.narrative: Maximizing Agricultural Revenue and Key Enterprises in Target Sites (MARKETS)

description.narrative: USAID/Nigerias Maximizing Agricultural Revenue and Key Enterprises in Targeted Sites (MARKETS) was a multi-faceted six and a half-year pilot program designed to strengthen agricultural competitiveness and food security in Nigeria. MARKETS employed a private sector-led, comprehensive value chain approach that identified commercial buyers and facilitated inputs that supported farmers to meet market standards and a guaranteed buyer.

title.narrative: Lafiya – Health Resilience of North East Nigeria (HeRON)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Support at least 83 health facilities and seven nutrition stabilization centers across 23 LGAs (13 in Borno and 10 in Yobe). .Focus on integration of quality of care into the basic Primary Health Care package to ensure that basic package of services is available and accessible;.Procure essential medicines and supplies while coordinating and leveraging Government of Nigeria and existing donors' investments supporting Malaria, Family Planning, HIV/TB, and nutrition commodities; .Build on the existing pool of trainers established during the past two years, an integrated competency focused on-the-job mentoring and coaching approach will be adopted, with facility-based training in a low-dose high-frequency approach; and .Transition internally displaced persons in select IDP camps in Adamawa state from emergency humanitarian aid dependency to independent self-sustaining residents..Integrate WASH activities into health programming by promoting the adoption of essential WASH actions, food and environmental hygiene including handwashing, and safe disposal of medical waste at the health facility levels.The overall purpose of the Health Resilience in Northeast Nigeria (HeRON) activity (previously known as the Northeast Health Transition Program) is to save lives and reduce suffering for the poorest and most vulnerable in North-East Nigeria, through a stronger and more resilient health system. This activity contributes directly to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2, the Embassy's ICS, and is closely aligned with Goal 3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan...

title.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Palliative Care: Basic Health Care and Support - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

description.narrative: PEPFAR: HIV/AIDS - Basic health care and support, which includes: all clinic-based and home/community-based activities for HIV-infected adults, children, and their families that are aimed at optimizing the quality of life for HIV-infected clients and their families throughout the continuum of illness by the means of symptom diagnosis and relief, psychological and spiritual support, clinical monitoring, related laboratory services and management of opportunistic infections (excluding TB) and other HIV/AIDS-related complications (including pharmaceuticals), and culturally-appropriate end-of-life care. Basic health care and support also includes clinic-based and home/community-based support, social and material support such as nutrition support, legal aid, and housing, and training and support of caregivers. Clinic-based and home/community-based care and support activities for HIV-positive children within programs for orphans and other vulnerable children affected by HIV/AIDS would fall under sub-element 1.1.8 (Orphans and Vulnerable Children). ARV treatment should be coded under sub-element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and sub-element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services). - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

title.narrative: Protecting the Drug Supply Chain with an Affordable and Handy Innovation

description.narrative: In low- and middle-income countries, 50 million children under five years old are at risk of not achieving their developmental potential. Studies suggest that the education level of parents may positively influence their childrens development, but this causal link has not been proven. If true, then investing in secondary education today would improve outcomes for future generations. The implementing partner is conducting a randomized controlled trial to compare the early childhood development outcomes of children in Ghana whose parents were randomly selected in 2008 to receive secondary school scholarships versus the outcomes of the children of parents in the control group. This research presents a unique opportunity to combine current measures of child development with over ten years of data from earlier trials. This award will generate evidence to inform policymakers about the intergenerational returns to universal access to secondary education and potentially benefit 6 million secondary school students in the first five years.

title.narrative: Scaling a Digital Approach to Targeted Malaria Treatment

description.narrative: Private sector pharmacies and clinics are a significant provider of healthcare in many parts of Africa; however, quality care and treatments are often scarce. Patients frequently choose the lowest-cost pathway to treatment, skipping over diagnostic testing and purchasing cheaper, poor-quality options. For example, in private pharmacies, fewer than one in ten suspected malaria cases are tested to confirm a diagnosis; studies have found that more than 65 percent of sales of a common antimalarial drug are by people who do not have malaria, fueling overtreatment while leaving patients untreated for other illnesses. To increase appropriately targeted care, Maisha Meds developed a digital inventory and sales management platform for pharmacies. The platform includes a voluntary loyalty program allowing Maisha Meds to offer targeted reimbursements to both patients and pharmacists to incentivize using a rapid diagnostic test for malaria, followed by quality antimalarials only for those with a test confirming malaria diagnosis. A Stage 2 award (20192022) from Development Innovation Ventures (DIV) enabled Maisha Meds to expand its platform from 200 to more than 1,000 pharmacies in Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda and conduct a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effect of the loyalty program on appropriate antimalarial use. The trial found a 300 percent increase in appropriate malaria case management compared to the control group; the program significantly increased sales of rapid diagnostic tests and increased the percentage of antimalarials sold with a confirmatory diagnosis while decreasing the number of antimalarials sold without a confirmatory diagnosis. With new support from DIV, Maisha Meds aims to expand its network of pharmacies using the platform to 2,500 additional facilities, serving 400,000 patients through the loyalty program across Nigeria, Kenya, and Uganda. title.narrative: Testing a Digital Platform and Incentives to Deliver Child Health Care

description.narrative: Dimagi developed CommCare Connect (CCC) to encourage frontline workers to reach children in high-need areas, Through CCC, which is built on Dimagis CommCare platform, locally led healthcare organizations fulfill pay-per-service delivery contracts under which frontline workers rapidly learn, deliver, and are paid for verified high-impact services. CCC improves the efficiency of tracking and verifying high-impact health interventions, such as Vitamin A supplementation and oral rehydration salts (ORS) to treat diarrhoeal dehydration, which have been found to significantly reduce child mortality. With DIV support, Dimagi will refine how CCC supports child health campaigns and to conduct a randomized controlled trial to evaluate whether it is more cost-effective than the status quo in delivering Vitamin A and ORS to children under five in northern Nigeria, where GiveWell is funding a CCC expansion.

Testing a biometric identification system to improve malaria vaccine rates. Testing a Biometric Identification System to Improve Malaria Vaccine Rates is a new impact evaluation project that will measure the impact of Simprints solution: a digital vaccination record system linked to biometrics which automatically identifies children who have missed a vaccine, and sends voice message reminders to caregivers.

Improve the capacity of businesses to integrate into domestic and international markets through increases in productivity and improvements in corporate governance and the development and application of modern technology and marketing practices. Enhance the capacity of businesses and business associations in terms of their corporate governance capabilities and their application of best practices and technologies to achieve increased production and marketing of products and services. It includes adoption of efficient production processes, improved labor productivity, environmentally-sound management of natural resources and the development of accounting and management systems that can help the company and industry group implement business, labor, product and process standards that enhance business competitiveness. Business capacity development programs may include activities that help men- and women-owned firms and associations respond to these international markets and create regional alliances.

title.narrative: Community Health Worker-led Participatory Learning and Action

description.narrative: To strengthen the uptake of effective neonatal care practices, such as thermal care, skin-to-skin contact and care-seeking for sick newborns, some countries have adopted the Participatory Learning and Action (PLA) model. In the PLA model, trained facilitators convene community groups of women who are pregnant or of reproductive age to identify maternal and newborn health challenges, and develop and implement localized strategies to improve health practices. FHI 360 and its partners Ekjut and University College London (UCL) will work with the governments of Mozambique and Nigeria to replicate a Community Health Workers (CHW)-led version of the PLA model that has previously been tested and scaled in India. In a DIV-funded RCT, the partners will assess the impact of the locally adapted intervention on the neonatal mortality rate and adoption of highimpact practices, and assess the programs feasibility and cost-effectiveness. The purpose of the Nigeria Third Party Monitoring Project (NTPMP) contract is to provide independent, verifiable, primary data regarding the outputs and quality of humanitarian assistance activities funded by the United States Agency for International Developments Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (USAID/BHA) in Nigeria through comprehensive third-party monitoring (TPM). TPM is necessary to ensure USAID/BHA has sufficient information to perform oversight and accountability of implementing partner (IP) activities. Due to the non-permissive environment in Nigeria and the inability of USAID/BHA staff to travel to activity implementation sites, TPM is essential to fulfill this purpose. USAID/BHA will use TPM information provided by the NTPMP to identify issues and challenges related to the delivery of goods and services, potential large-scale aid diversion, accountability to affected populations, and make real-time programmatic adjustments and inform future programmatic decisions and designs.

description.narrative: (Nigeria): .The Addressing Education in Northeast Nigeria (AENN) activity addresses acute emergency education needs in two states, Borno and Yobe, affected by Boko Haram and Islamic State in West Africa, while laying the foundation to rebuild and transform these states' education systems. This aims to redress long-standing education grievances related to the insurgency while building trust in Nigerian education institutions. Many out of school girls and boys, ages 6-15, including some who will gain school access for the first time, will benefit from equitable access to certified high-quality basic education opportunities. In collaboration with the respective Nigerian state governments and other donor partners, USAID and its implementing partner will identify specific Local Government Areas in the targeted states using information collected through the Rapid Education and Risk Analysis process conducted at the beginning of the activity..Planned interventions include: enhancing education authorities' capacity to plan, manage and oversee education services; providing safe education opportunities and instructional materials; preparing teachers to deliver conflict-sensitive, quality basic education instruction; and training and revitalization of community coalitions.....

title.narrative: Effective Water Sanitation and Hygiene Services (E-WASH) Task Order under the Water and Development IQC

description.narrative: The United States Agency for International Development (USAID) is partnering with RTI International to improve urban water service delivery in Nigeria. The Effective Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene Services (E-WASH) program works to ensure sustainable water services through better governance and accountability, as well as policy, institutional, and regulatory reform. The program aims to increase access to basic drinking water supplies for 500,000 households in six states across the country. The E-WASH program aims to improve performance of six State Water Boards (SWBs) by strengthening core financial and operational capabilities to increase services, attract outside investment, and reduce water losses throughout the system. Well-functioning SWBs will result in increased access to sustainable WASH services. Simultaneously, E-WASHs civil society engagement activities will encourage participation and collaboration with the SWBs, as well as catalyze innovation for better water and sanitation services. Throughout its activities, the E-WASH program will focus on sustainability and equal access for women, the poor and marginalized groups.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Nigeria Integrated Agricultural Activity

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds, activity will:.Support the scale up of interventions in the current focus states of Adamawa and Borno and expand the community seed production into the additional states of Gombe and Yobe. These intervention will include: Identifying 2,250 seed producers to become Community Based Seed Entrepreneurs (CBSE) and Establishing 150 CBSE cooperatives consisting of a minimum of 15-20 members; Develop and roll out a profitable and sustainable seed production and supply system and design appropriate business models needed for CBSE to sell certified seeds to smallholder farmers in the local markets; and Promote good crop varieties and management practices that are best suited for each agro-ecology in the selected states. This activity will contribute to the economic recovery in Northeast Nigeria in the wake of the devastation caused by the ongoing insurgency in the region, focusing on supporting vulnerable populations disenfranchised by the conflict and seeking to re-engage them in basic farming activities. The activity promotes climate-smart agriculture that aims to increase agricultural productivity and strengthened capacity to withstand shocks and stresses, which include those that are as a result of climate change. This activity contributes to addressing the challenges and obstacles holding back the agricultural, health, and nutrition sectors through inclusive, gender-sensitive, and sustainable agricultural-led economic growth. The activity directly contributes to the Mission's FtF strategy as well as Goal 1 and 2 of the Joint Strategic Plan. The activity will promote bio fortified seeds (such as vitamin A fortified maize, zinc fortified rice, and iron fortified cowpea) to enable CBSE to cultivate bio fortified crops. Also the activity will facilitate diversification and increase production of nutrient-dense crops, including processing, storage, preservation, and market expansion for vulnerable groups, particularly for nutritious foods....

title.narrative: Feed the Future Nigeria Agribusiness Investment Activity

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The Feed the Future Agribusiness Investment Activity continues to increase the agricultural competitiveness of Nigeria's smallholder farmers by addressing constraints within the business environment in Nigeria and increasing agriculture-related investment. The activity comprises three main components: 1) increasing the ease of doing business; 2) increasing access to finance; and 3) spurring investment promotion. Overall, the activity improves the agribusiness investment climate, which plays a pivotal role in attracting foreign direct and domestic investments. It also prioritizes partnerships with private sector actors in targeted states. Nutrition-related businesses, such as those involved in the manufacture of nutrient-rich foods, continue to benefit under this activity. The activity contributes to the Mission's Feed the Future strategy, which seeks to improve the competitiveness of smallholder farmers and the Administration's priority of helping Nigerian farmers become self-reliant. These outcomes will be achieved through training, technical assistance, establishing strong working relationships with relevant entities in the public and private sector, and leveraging relationships with investment firms (private equity, venture capital and impact investors) and lead agribusinesses..Through training and clinics, the activity works with local and international business development specialists to build capacity and provide support to women entrepreneurs and women's associations, including the Women Farmers Advancement Network and the Nigerian Women Agro-Allied Farmers Association.......

(Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Deploy security resource tools, instant communication tools, site visits, training, and regular meetings to USAID Nigeria contractors and sub-contractors;.Assist with the effective delivery of U.S. government funded assistance; .Strengthen the ability of IPs to prepare for potential security incidents; and .Keep IPs abreast of security situations as they unfold in Nigeria. .USAID/Nigeria has established a Partner Liaison Security Operation (PLSO). The PLSO facilitates communications between USAID Implementing Partners (IPs) operating in Nigeria. PLSO allows IPs to effectively use and share publicly available security information, thereby improving their security situational awareness. The PLSO activity (supported by USAID's Automated Directives System (ADS) 573) is implemented in countries identified as high threat posts, such as Nigeria..PLSO produces weekly activity reports for the Mission and USAID/Washington on security incidents throughout the country. This activity permits all FY 2022 funded activities to implement with additional security resources and information at their disposal to reduce security incidents and help keep partners and staff safe..

title.narrative: Sharing the Green Grass: Cultivating a Locally-led Peace Architecture in the Niger Delta.

description.narrative: The project aims to strengthen local capacities to peacefully manage conflict and prevent violence from escalating within a locally-led peace architecture in the Niger Delta. The project pursues two specific objectives: Farmer and herder communities cultivate the skills and relationships to collaborate on peace and security issues and Farmer and herder communities develop effective, sustainable local mechanisms for early warning response, dispute management, and violence mitigation.

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 Funds this activity will:Support capacity building of Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and state independent electoral; Provide technical assistance to further improve the capacity and commitment of INEC and other election management bodies to deliver credible elections through means such as improved accuracy of the voter register;Sustain improvement of new technology (e.g. biometric card readers); improved internal efficiency and knowledge management; andImprove voter education outreach to marginalized populations (women, youth, persons with disabilities, and internally displaced persons).In preparation for local government elections and off-cycle elections that will take place before and immediately after the scheduled general elections this activity will reinforce the capacity of INEC and other election management bodies to conduct free, fair, transparent, and peaceful elections, thus leading to improved public confidence in Nigeria's democracy and further promote the credibility and sustainability of electoral institutions. Targeted technical assistance will be used to strengthen the capacity of INEC and other election management bodies to help ensure credible electoral processes are critical to strengthening good governance in Nigeria. Strengthening democratic governance is a key priority of the Integrated Country Strategy for Nigeria, the USAID CDCS, and directly supports Goal 4 of the 2022-20226 Joint Strategic Plan..

(Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:Build the capacity of religious and traditional leaders, as well as women and youth, to promote tolerance and prevent violent conflict and extremism in their communities;Foster the rights of religious and ethnic minorities by initiating various interventions to address interethnic and interreligious conflict; andWork with local stakeholders to create and support community-based early warning, early response (EWER) systems.The Community Initiatives to Promote Peace (CIPP) activity implements quick impact initiatives aimed at bringing communities together to promote peace and stability in Benue, Kaduna, Kano, Katsina, Kogi, and Plateau states. This activity will work with Nigerian government institutions (such as the Human Rights Commission) and private sector actors at all levels to build the sustainability of early response systems and strengthen the capacity of relevant organizations to identify and address religious issues. Maintaining gender-sensitive methodologies and gender integration, the activity also elevates women's unique role in preventing and mitigating conflict by integrating women leaders into local community- and state-level peace structures. These actions will strengthen the capacity of communities to promote communal resilience against conflict and religious freedom in target states. These results align with key priorities of the Integrated Country Strategy for Nigeria and are key U.S. foreign policy priorities for the region, specifically Goals 1-3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan..

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Provide health system support to the Bauchi State Government to plan, budget and coordinate the implementation of primary health care services in the state and advocate for improved health system governance and domestic resource mobilization. .Build the capacity of the health care workers (private & public) to provide equitable, quality primary health services and to reach underserved populations; .Issue small grants to local organizations to provide technical assistance and capacity building to support health facilities in provision of nutrition services, gender based violence (GBV) and informal sector enrollment in financial risk protection schemes; and .Promote the adoption of essential WASH actions such as handwashing and safe disposal of waste at the facility levels in Bauchi State. .This activity will strengthen health systems and increase access to and improve the quality of primary health care services in supported states in Nigeria. Interventions work in Bauchi State to support a multipartite MOU between the Bauchi State Government, USAID Nigeria, Gates Foundation, Global Affairs Canada, Dangote Foundation, and UNICEF. It aims to reduce maternal and child mortality in Bauchi, and to increase public and private health systems' skills to sustainably supervise and manage quality primary health care services. .This activity contributes to USAID priorities by focusing on evidence-based interventions, sustainability, localization and capacity building. It also contributes to USAID priorities by focusing on evidence-based interventions, sustainability, and capacity building. It also contributes directly to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2, the Embassy's ICS, and is closely aligned with Goal 3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan..

title.narrative: Feed the Future Nigeria Agricultural Extension and Advisory Services and Technology Promotion Activity

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY2022 funds, this activity will:.Strengthen sustainable agricultural extension and advisory services to reach at least two million smallholder farmers and other actors in agricultural value chains. Build the capacity of private extension service providers to deliver extension and advisory services capably and sustainably to smallholder farmers, and Strengthen linkages between agricultural research institutions and agriculture value chain stakeholders. Through technical assistance, training linked to inputs and outputs markets, and increasing access to finance, the activity will work with a variety of agricultural sector micro, small, and medium enterprises, importers, financial and insurance institutions, and government agencies to ensure that high quality agricultural inputs efficiently pass through the agro-input supply chain via private extension services providers and into the hands of farmers when they are needed. By stimulating inclusive, innovative, and pluralistic agricultural extension services, developing the capacity of agro-input suppliers and service providers, and facilitating the adoption of new technologies and improved production practices by smallholder farmers, the activity contributes to the Mission's Feed the Future strategy as well as Goal 1 and 2 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan. The activity will enable households to make informed production, marketing, and spending decisions--thereby making safe and nutritious foods more available, affordable, and accessible. The activity also promotes climate-smart agriculture, affordable, safe, and nutritious foods through technologies such as reducing contaminants in grains. The activity will link women and youth to digital financial services, offer training, internships, and enable women and youth to become entrepreneurs, employers or self-employed agro-dealers, or village promoters who develop solutions to address unequal access to land, inputs, finance, and extension services....

(Nigeria): .. .With FY 2022 funds this activity will:Strengthen governance systems (with a focus on public financial management and procurement, as well as monitoring and evaluation) related to the delivery of services in key sectors; Increase government responsiveness to citizen needs and priorities including provision of services; andImprove government and civil society capacity to manage conflict.This activity will address some of the principal underlying conditions stifling economic growth, stunting human development, and fueling conflict in Nigeria including: poor governance, corruption, weak institutions, and limited basic service delivery at the state and local levels.This multi-sectoral activity will work with selected states and local governments to improve the governance of primary health care and basic education services with emphasis placed on strengthening linkages and information exchange between government units. By enhancing the capacity of local civil society partners to monitor government performance, hold local authorities accountable for prudent expenditure of public resources, and improve the delivery of key services via emphasis on good governance, State2State will improve government responsiveness to citizen needs. Lack of services and inability of government to assist citizens is a driving force of instability in NE and NW Nigeria resulting in conflict, banditry and the disenfranchisement of the general population. This activity aligns closely to key priorities of the Integrated Country Strategy for Nigeria, USAID's CDCS and Goals 1-3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Nigeria Rural Resilience Activity

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will: .Assist Nigerian farmers to recover from shocks and stresses;.Facilitate economic recovery for vulnerable households; and.Work with farmers and non-farm actors (such as input suppliers, aggregators, and processors) to develop market linkages, improve agricultural productivity, and promote non-farm enterprise opportunities. .Interventions will focus on women's empowerment to improve nutrition results, boost agricultural growth and productivity, and improve farm and non-farm livelihoods among the most vulnerable to increase economic opportunities for men, women, and youth. This activity will directly benefit over 560,000 individuals across the four northeast states of Adamawa, Borno, Gombe, and Yobe. .The activity operates on the premise that stimulating inclusive resilient market systems, that take into account the challenges and constraints of the Northeast operating environment, will systemically move individuals and households out of chronic vulnerability and improve the Northeast's economy. This transformation will set Nigeria on a path for increased stability, resilience, prosperity, and market inclusion. The activity will work within carefully selected value chains that have the potential to drive both economic expansion and inclusion. .The activity contributes to the Mission's Feed the Future strategy and JSP GOALS 1 and 2. The activity's workforce development programs, mentorship, and leadership training will target women and youth to build their capacity and skills while preparing them for greater leadership roles in their communities. This approach enables individuals and communities to engage in strong and sustainable market systems rather than continuing to rely on humanitarian assistance. The activity promotes climate-smart agriculture to strengthen the capacity to withstand shocks and stresses, which include those that are as a result of climate change....

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:Expand and strengthen coverage of both facility and community interventions; Improve diagnostics including the optimizing new tools to match the increased number of people to be tested;Reach underserved communities in hard to reach areas; and Strategically increase public-private mix coverage.This activity will increase the number of TB patients detected, treated, and notified of their status in 14 states (Bauchi, Kaduna, Katsina, Kano, Nasarawa, Plateau, Taraba, Anambra, Akwa Ibom, Benue, Cross River, Delta, Imo, and Rivers). It will also strengthen public private partnerships and alliances with health and related professional organizations, including faith-based associations, to influence their constituencies and communities to implement TB control interventions. This activity will serve as a platform to expand TB care, treatment, and notification services to all public and private health facilities in target states and will facilitate the accomplishment of statewide TB screening and treatment targets. It will also leverage TB platforms to support equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines for all eligible persons in seven selected states. The activity will partner with federal and state ministries of health and other relevant government agencies, as well as the formal and informal private health sector to screen 9,185,965 persons for TB and diagnose and treat 54,978 TB patients. The activity will continue to build the capacity of the national and state TB programs to conduct real-time surveillance for TB patients and establish links to quality care and treatment programs.This activity contributes directly to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2 and is closely aligned with Goal 1 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan...

description.narrative: (Nigeria): ...With FY 2022 funds this activity will: .Expand access to water and sanitation facilities and improve the governance of water resources in small communities in Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) in Northeast Nigeria and Abia, Delta, and Imo State in the southern part of the country; and. Funds will be utilized for on-going construction in the Northeast, and will mobilize resources to the south of Nigeria to improve the water treatment plants in Abia, Delta and Imo states. .This activity will provide technical assistance, address immediate sanitation needs and challenges related to Fecal Sludge Management (FSM) by supporting the construction of a Fecal Sludge Treatment Facility and strengthening Emergency FSM models and rehabilitate three water supply systems to supply water to approximately 60,000 households in Abia, Imo, and Delta states. This activity will facilitate the economic recovery of some crisis-affected communities and bolster the capacity of the state governments in providing essential WASH services by creating and sustaining enabling environments for Small Towns Water Supply and Sanitation Agencies and Water Consumers Associations to operate effectively. The activity will support climate change adaptation or mitigation objectives in its water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) programming..This activity contributes to the CDCS Development Objective 1: Broadened and Inclusive Economic Growth and Intermediate Result (IR) 1.4: Water resource management and services improved. This activity links directly to JSP Goals 1 and 2 and water strategies... .

title.narrative: USAID Youth-Powered Ecosystem to Advance Urban Adolescent Health and Well-Being (YPE4AH)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Strengthen adolescent access to youth-friendly RH/FP and nutrition services;.Ensure the Youth Hubs and surrounding facilities continue to be operated as safe spaces for adolescents; .Provide training, internship and apprenticeship opportunities for adolescents by leveraging private sector support and opportunities; and.Build the capacity of three local partners to increasingly play an important role in the management cycle of USAID and other partners' development efforts, furthering USAID's localization efforts..Youth Powered Ecosystem to Advance Urban Adolescent Health (YPE4AH) is a five-year cooperative agreement designed through a co-creation process to empower young Nigerians to access the skills, social capital, and resources needed to realize their futures. This activity will improve the health and well-being of urban, underprivileged, out-of-school, and unmarried adolescents (especially girls) aged 15-19 by increasing voluntary family planning (FP) uptake and continued use. The activity focuses on designated Youth Hubs which are safe spaces for youth to seek and access FP and reproductive health (RH) information and referrals in urban slums, in four Local Government Areas (LGAs) in Kano and Lagos States. These are the two largest urban areas in the country and reflect diverse cultural and socioeconomic contexts, providing an opportunity to inform adaptation to different zones and scale-up for greater impact. The activity has adapted and is scaling up evidence-based, high-impact SKILLZ curricula (a skills-building program), which combines sports, fun-based activities and group sessions led by youth coaches, age 20-28, to spur healthy behavior change and to shift attitudes towards more equitable gender norms. .This activity contributes directly to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2, the Embassy's ICS, and is closely aligned with Goal 3 of the Joint Strategic Plan...

title.narrative: Strengthening Civic Advocacy and Local Engagement (SCALE)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:Strengthen the financial, management and advocacy capacity of local civil society organizations (CSOs) and business management organizations (BMOs);Improve the managerial and advocacy capacity of CSOs to drive policy change and greater public accountability; andProvide technical assistance on countering trafficking-in-persons, and to support grants to local organizations advocating for improved policies in the key sectors.This activity will strengthen partnerships between CSO-led coalitions and networks, targeted Government of Nigeria institutions, and key stakeholders to advocate for and monitor selected development reforms aimed at increasing government systems' transparency, accountability, and responsiveness to achieve higher quality social services in key sectors. Key sectors include health (maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH), population, nutrition, HIV/AIDS, and TB), education (disbursement and transparency in the use of universal basic education funds), economic growth, disability, gender equality/women's empowerment, sexual and gender-based violence, countering trafficking-in-persons, and child early marriage. For example, this activity will work through CSO coalitions and networks to advocate for budgetary allocation and funds expenditure related to MNCH and provide oversight of available MNCH resources by promoting transparency and accountability principles thereby ensuring value for money. This activity aligns closely with USAID Nigeria's CDCS and supports Goal 1-3 of the 2022-20226 Joint Strategic Plan... .

The Strengthening HIV/AIDS Response Partnership and Evidenced-Based Results (SHARPER) initiative, funded by the U.S. Agency for International Development, is designed to reduce HIV transmission among the most-at-risk populations, including people living with HIV and their sex partners, female and male sex workers and men who have sex with men

Through USAIDs Nigeria Strategic HIV/AIDS and TB Response Program (SHARP), Chemonics is leading Nigeria SHARP Task Orders 3 to improve HIV and TB services to over 145 health facilities across 11 states in northern Nigeria.

title.narrative: Integrated Health Program (IHP) Task Order Seven (TO7)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Advance the goals of a bilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) held by USAID and the FCT, outlining both parties' roles in contributing to the reduction of maternal and child mortality and increasing the health system capacity to sustainably support quality PHC services;.Utilize low-dose, high-frequency training, delivered through grants under contracts, and supportive supervision to strengthen clinical competencies for health workers and improve service quality for reproductive; maternal; newborn; child and adolescent health; and nutrition at primary and secondary levels. Support will extend to one PHC in each of the 62 wards, 14 general hospitals, and 62 private clinics across all six area councils;.Strengthen FCT health systems such as the development and tracking of the 2023 harmonized health operational plan; continued roll out of the FCT Basic Health Care Provision Fund and Health Management Information Systems to ensure government partners have critical information for results-oriented, data-driven decisions; and incorporation of gender transformative approaches and the promotion of essential WASH actions such as environmental hygiene, handwashing and safe waste disposal at the facility level..This activity focuses on evidence-based reproductive, maternal, newborn, and child health interventions, sustainability, and capacity building, thus contributing to USAID/Nigeria's health and development objective of a healthier, more educated population in targeted states. It will strengthen health systems, increase access to and improve the quality of primary health care (PHC) in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). It also contributes to USAID priorities by focusing on evidence-based interventions, sustainability, localization and capacity building. This activity contributes directly to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2, the ICS, and Goal 3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan..

title.narrative: Integrated Health Program (IHP) Task Order Six (TO6)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Scale up high impact interventions in 171 primary health care units A(PHCs), 27 private/mission health facilities, and 14 secondary health facilities; .Expand access to integrated reproductive, maternal, newborn, child, adolescent health and nutrition (RMNCAH+N) services and bring services closer to communities;.Support monthly joint supportive supervisory visits with the Local Government Health Authority tailored to priority PHCs; .Provide technical support to relevant agencies to effectively implement the Basic Healthcare Provision Fund and the State Health Equity Fund to reach the most vulnerable with basic health services; and.Focus on skills transfer to strengthen the quality of services, data quality and use, and commodities management through clinical mentoring, coaching and support nutrition specific actions within the health facilities and outreach programs in communities.. Integrate WASH activities into health programming to support maternity services and improved service delivery..This activity will contribute to reductions in child and maternal morbidity and mortality and increase the capacity of health systems (public and private) to sustainably support quality PHC services for RMNCAH+N in Ebonyi State as part of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) signed between USAID and the State government on PHC revitalization. It will work in 13 Local Government Areas and support the state to update a harmonized 2023 annual operational plan based on prior performance reviews and lessons learned and will include evidence-based budgeting for 2023. This activity contributes to USAID priorities by focusing on evidence-based interventions, sustainability, localization and capacity building. It contributes to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2, the Embassy's ICS, and is closely aligned with Goal 3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan..

title.narrative: U.S. President’s Malaria Initiative for States Task Order 4 (TO4)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Provide technical assistance, training, and small grants to local organizations to: 1) build capacity for the management of malaria prevention and case management in public and private health facilities; 2) prevent malaria in pregnancy, including providing intermittent preventive malaria therapy for pregnant women; 3) strengthen health systems for service delivery, including supervision and monitoring; and 4) improve reporting and quality of health data from service delivery points; and.Improve malaria case management and expand access to services that prevent malaria in pregnancy..Malaria contributes significantly to morbidity and mortality of children and pregnant women. The United States is a major partner in efforts to fight the malaria scourge in Nigeria which has a national average prevalence of 23 percent (Demographic and Health Survey, 2018). This activity implements in Zamfara, Nasarawa, Benue, and Plateau states, serving an estimated 18 million people. .This activity will lead to increased utilization of quality health services in target areas and population groups and contribute to USAID priorities by focusing on evidence-based interventions, sustainability, and capacity building. This activity contributes directly to USAID Nigeria CDCS Development Objective 2, the Embassy's ICS, and is closely aligned with Goal 3 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan..

The HWM Activity works in Bauchi, Sokoto, Kebbi, and Ebonyi States as well as the Federal Capital Territory. The HWM purpose is to establish a costeffective, well-trained, and motivated health workforce, particularly in targeted rural and remote areas in order to contribute to greater health systems responsiveness and improved health outcomes, especially among women and children. The HWM objectives are to: 1) Strengthen the pre-service training learning environment and in-service training program; 2) Support the building of a robust human resources information system to keep track of recruitment, deployment, retention, and continuing education; 3) Strengthen governance and management of the health workforce; and, 4) Support the conduct of human resources for health (HRH) research to improve HRH practices and retention mechanisms.

description.narrative: Data management services for evaluation and monitoring support.

(Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will:.Provide cross-sectoral, Mission-wide support on strategy, project, and activity-level monitoring, evaluation, and learning; and.Provide third-party, field-based monitoring, and data gathering to augment the Mission's evidence base for accountability and decision making..Due to increasing insecurity across the country, strict Embassy security restrictions for chief of mission staff, and a generalised non-permissive implementation environment traditionally monitoring, evaluation, and learning has become difficult. The goal of the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Support Activity (MELSA) activity is to provide third party MEL tools to staff and partners and help transform USAID/Nigeria into a premier practitioner of program monitoring and evaluation rooted in organizational learning and adaptation. MELSA will provide continuous, on-the-ground, on-demand and systematic support to all USAID/Nigeria technical teams and implementing partners on performance monitoring, data verification, performance and impact evaluations, project- and activity-level monitoring, evaluation and learning plans, organizational learning, capacity building, short term technical assistance, and knowledge management. This activity cross-cuts the USAID Nigeria CDCS supporting all objectives as well as being closely aligned with Goals 1- 4 of the 2022-2026 Joint Strategic Plan...

(Nigeria): WIth FY 2022 funds this activity will:Build the capacity of civil society organizations (CSOs) to conduct domestic election monitoring and voter education, focused on election results, electoral violence, and access to electoral processes for marginalized groups including women, youth, persons with disabilities, and internally displaced persons. Support the recruitment and training of domestic monitors that will conduct traditional observation and deploy parallel vote tabulations for off-cycle elections. Through these interventions, USAID will strengthen the technical, organizational, and political support of key organizations actively engaged in Nigeria's electoral system to help produce credible outcomes and long-term sustainability of electoral processes in Nigeria. More credible electoral and political processes contribute to strengthening good governance in Nigeria, which is a key priority of the Integrated Country Strategy for Nigeria, the USAID CDCS, and directly supports Goal 4 of the 2022-20226 Joint Strategic Plan..

title.narrative: Strengthening Deaf Education, Empowerment and Employment (Deaf-E³)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): ..To address the needs of deaf, hard of hearing, and deafblind (D/HH/DB) children and youth in Nigeria, the Deaf-E³ activity will build the capacity of multiple community and professional groups: educational professionals, D/HH/DB community members and leaders, sign language interpreters, development professionals, and parents of D/HH/DB children. This will be accomplished by: (a) Providing educational professionals with training in a multimodal/multilingual pedagogical approach and co-developing two manuals on this approach, to be shared with additional professionals; (b) Developing the Nigerian National Association of the Deaf (NNAD) organizational capacity and the individual capacity of its stakeholders, and the involvement of D/HH/DB role models in educational settings with professionals, families, and their D/HH/DB children; (c) Establishing a working group of Nigerian Sign Language interpreters and deaf consumers that will analyze current and best practices related to interpreting as a whole and specific to education; and, (d) Increasing the capacity of USAID and its partners to engage D/HH/DB stakeholders nationwide, as well as enlisting support from these development actors in promoting awareness of NNAD as a resource to parents, government ministries, and others in the field of education, amplifying this activity's impact on the lives of D/HH/DB people in Nigeria....

The U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) through Partners for Development launched a Water Improvement and Sanitation Enhancement (WISE) activity to improve water safety in Jigawa and Kano states. The WISE activity will reduce the occurrence and impact of waterborne diseases through improvements in access to clean drinking water and sanitation, and the adoption of key hygiene behaviors. One of the first tasks will be to construct or rehabilitate 30 water access points and install 55 sanitation facilities in schools and community health centers. These improved water access points will provide clean drinking water to more than 66,000 local residents.

title.narrative: The Northern Education Initiative Plus (NEI+) Activity

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The Northern Education Initiative Plus (NEI+) activity addresses low literacy rates and mitigates causes of conflict in Northern Nigeria by assisting Bauchi and Sokoto states to increase access to basic education, especially for girls and Out-of-School-Children (OOSC). It aims to significantly improve reading outcomes for more than 1.4 million school-aged children. Activities include training teachers and learning facilitators in formal schools and non-formal learning centers, strengthening school-based management committees and civil society organizations, and persuading parents to enroll their children in local schools; and providing textbooks and learning materials. By working with four state Colleges of Education to include early grade reading concepts, techniques, practices, and materials in their curriculum, the activity will continue to build state capacity to deliver effective reading instruction. This will improve reading proficiency for 900,000 school-aged children in grades 1 to 3, and 500,000 out of school children in non-formal learning settings. In its final years of implementation, NEI+ will emphasize mainstreaming successful graduates, ages 6-11, into their local primary schools... ...

(Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds this activity will: .Improve reading outcomes for pupils in grades 1-3 in select Nigerian states; .Strengthen the capacity of the Nigerian basic education system to expand and replicate evidence-based reading practices that promote quality teaching and learning, especially for girls and those from disadvantaged groups; and.Provide students with the foundational skills and abilities to progress to higher levels of education and become self-reliant citizens..In FY 2022, LEARN to Read partnered with federal, state, and local education officials to improve pre-service and in-service teacher capacity, and develop policies that strengthen the enabling environment for sustainable education reforms.This activity includes a small grants component to engage youth, especially young girls, in education development in their communities..LEARN to Read activity focus is on foundational learning including reading skills of pupils, especially girls, in grades 1 and 2 in the conflict affected northern states of Bauchi, Sokoto and Adamawa. A rapid gender assessment was conducted and the evaluation will include disaggregation of all people level indicators by sex and age cohort at minimum. In 2022, gender and inclusion training was conducted for LEARN staff. The activity partners with other states to access services and technical assistance to deliver evidence-based reading instruction in the early grades. ..... ...

title.narrative: Watershed Management for Source Water Protection - NPI

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 fund this activity will:.Improve the availability of safe drinking water and gender-responsive sanitation facilities; The activity will strengthen long-term access to safe drinking water and reduce levels of water-borne disease by supporting community-based interventions on watershed governance and sanitation and protecting watershed sources through conserving forest and woodland ecosystems..Strengthen community and civil society organization engagement in the management of their natural resources and watersheds through increased engagement and technical assistance;.Develop opportunities for economically viable and sustainable livelihoods through the rehabilitation if WASH infrastructure; and.Work closely with communities to ensure that protected areas serve as anchor institutions that maintain critical ecosystem services. .This activity will increase the water security and resilience of 137 communities, benefitting approximately 200,000 people and ecosystems that depend upon the Cross River Watershed in Cross River State and the Pai River Watershed in Bauchi State. Engaging a variety of stakeholders, this activity will rehabilitate dysfunctional WASH infrastructure, build new facilities, and develop support mechanisms for sustainability. This includes nature-based solutions, such as improved watershed management which have been underutilized yet have the potential to offer lasting, cost-effective improvements with multiple benefits for water resources, climate change adaptation, communities, ecosystems and up and down stream community livelihoods. This activity links directly to JSP Goals 1 and 2, as well as Administration climate and water strategies..

title.narrative: Accelerating Control of the HIV Epidemic in Nigeria (ACE)

description.narrative: The activity's purpose is to support relevant HIV/AIDS/TB service delivery, through a combination of direct service delivery support and technical assistance in Nigeria, across a variety of technical areas relevant to the continuum of prevention, care, and treatment of HIV infection. Goals include: A healthier, better educated population, improved health and disease outcomes of priority populations in targeted states. These objectives hinge on the hypothesis that if the capacity of health and education institutions and systems is increased, if access to equitable health and education services is increased, if the quality of health and education service provision is increased and improved, and if the government's commitment and capacity to mobilize more of its own resources is increased then Nigeria will become more self-sufficient and effective in its management of essential health and education services, which will contribute to a healthier, better educated population.

title.narrative: Transforming Health and Resilience for Individuals Through Vibrant Empowerment (THRIVE)

description.narrative: THRIVE is a cooperative agreement that contributes to achieving sustained epidemic control by improving the health and wellbeing of children living with HIV and reducing the risk of HIV infection among vulnerable children, adolescents, and caregivers. The activity will provide a suite of comprehensive services to build resilience and mitigate the multiple, layered vulnerabilities faced by these sub-populations. The activity will also contribute to closing gaps in Nigerias pediatric care and treatment cascade, supporting children and adolescents living with HIV (C/ALHIV) and HIV positive caregivers to access continuous treatment, improve their quality of life, remain on HIV treatment and reduce the risk of transmission. THRIVE is USAID/Nigerias mechanism for implementing PEPFAR funded programs for orphans and vulnerable children (OVC) and its delivery arm for community-focused health and social welfare services.

Justice Beyond Borders (JBB) is a mapping project of national laws on the most serious international crimes across 193 UN Member States. The JBB Project seeks to help all survivors understand where and how they can access justice and ensure that perpetrators have nowhere to hide. Achieving this means mobilizing as many countries as possible to adopt the laws that would allow them to investigate and prosecute the most serious international crimes, to ensure that survivors know and can exercise their rights, and to ensure that such laws are consistently and effectively implemented. Only then will accountability become the norm and impunity the exception.

Under GHAIN, FHI 360 led and managed a coalition of partner organizations that supported the Government of Nigeria in reducing the impact of HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis (TB) in select states by strengthening and expanding HIV/AIDS services. Across Nigeria, GHAIN worked to ensure that health care providers safely and effectively delivered HIV testing and counseling, prevention of mother-to-child transmission, antiretroviral therapy (ART) and TB services and treatment of opportunistic infections.

The ADVANCE program seeks to build the institutional and operational capacity of Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) throughout Nigeria to improve public decision making, local governance and project development for equitable socioeconomic growth.

title.narrative: HIV/AIDS - Host Country Strategic Information Capacity (HIV) - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

description.narrative: PEPFAR: HIV/AIDS - Exams, clinical monitoring, related laboratory services, treatment and prevention of tuberculosis in HIV basic health care settings (including pharmaceuticals), as well as screening and referral for HIV testing, and clinical care related to TB clinical settings. If TB programs provide other basic health care and support services such as clinical or psychosocial services, these services would be coded under sub-element 1.1.6 (Basic Health Care and Support). If TB programs expand to provide clients with anti-retroviral treatment (ART), such services would fall under Sub-Element 1.1.10 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Drugs) and Sub-Element 1.1.11 (HIV/AIDS Treatment and Anti-Retroviral Services). Note: General TB treatment, prevention, and related programming must be funded with CSH/Infectious Diseases funds directed for TB, not with HIV/AIDS funds. - Assistance for HIV/AIDS

title.narrative: Prevention Organizational Systems AIDS Care and Treatment (Pro-ACT)

description.narrative: The Prevention Organizational Systems AIDS Care and Treatment (Pro-ACT) project goal is to build the capacity of Nigeria's public, private, and community sectors for sustainable HIV and AIDS and Tuberculosis prevention, control, care and treatment. Management Sciences for Health (MSH) is implementing Pro-ACT project in five Nigerian States: Niger, Kwara, Kebbi, Sokoto, and Zamfara.

(Nigeria): -The Targeted States High Impact Project (TSHIP) will focus on strengthening the delivery of high-impact interventions at low cost to reduce maternal and child deaths and improve state and local government capacity to deliver and promote these interventions.-Health systems activities will include improving human resource planning and training, health logistics, health information systems, health infrastructure, the policy environment and community ownership. Interventions supported will include a wide variety of integrated community and facility-based primary health care programs, including promotion of family planning/child spacing as a method to improve maternal and child health.-In FY 2014, the activity will focus on a malaria bednet campaign in Sokoto State, further development of its community-based health worker program, improved political engagement, and extending the improvements seen in family planning, while looking for ways to improve performance in routine immunization and polio.

(Nigeria): -The WASH activity will partner with the public and private sector to increase access to safe drinking water and reduce morbidity and mortality due to water borne and sanitation-related illnesses.-To expand access to safe, affordable, and reliable water and sanitation services, the activity will partner with a local NGO. Interventions will include constructing hand-pump boreholes, ventilated improved pit latrines, urinals, rain harvesters, and hand-washing stations. In order to ensure sustainability, villagers are trained to maintain and repair the hand pumps and wash slabs. This training will also allow individuals to earn money by maintaining and repairing in other villages.-In addition, the activity will provide drinking water treatments and educate schools and communities on hygiene practices. The activity will also reinforce Support for Vulnerable Household, a Feed the Future activity in Sokoto State using the Multiple Use System approach which delivers water for drinking and other domestic uses.-This activity will help reduce water-related illnesses; reduce time spent by women and girls fetching water from distant and often polluted sources; and increase opportunities for girls' education and attendance.

title.narrative: Program to Build Leadership and Accountability in Nigeria health system (PLAN - Health)

description.narrative: The Program to Build Leadership and Accountability in Nigeria's Health System (PLAN-Health) is a five-year, President's Emergency Fund for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) associate award through the United States Agency for International Development (USAID). It is implemented by Management Sciences for Health (MSH) in Gombe and Akwa Ibom States and the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja. From commencement in 2010, the project aimed to strengthen the leadership and management capacities of 30 public sector health institutions (PSHIs) and civil society organizations (CSOs) for improved delivery of quality HIV and AIDS and other health services in Nigeria. PLAN-Health is assisting CSOs and PSHIs to become more adept at developing and maintaining the health services needed to meet health challenge targets by 2015. Through workshops, internships, embedded consultancies, technical assistance, coaching, and the PEPFAR Health Professionals Fellowship, PLAN-Health has helped to build strong and viable organizations by developing leadership skills and more capable managers.

description.narrative: (Nigeria): -The SIDHAS activity will provide quality TB and HIV/AIDS services and build the capacity of the public and private sectors in Nigeria to ensure sustainability.-SIDHAS will build on USAID TBHIV investments in three of the six priority states to expand facility and community based DOTS and DR TB services to unreached populations. description.narrative: (Nigeria): .The aim of STEER is to improve the wellbeing of OVCs in PEPFAR priority states by enabling them to fully access and utilize comprehensive and coordinated services. STEER will integrate TB services into its existing mandate in two states (Lagos and Akwa Ibom) by screening vulnerable children for TB, and linking them to designated diagnostic and treatment facilities. The project will develop and implement context-specific communication strategies in the communities where it works to improve awareness of TB...

title.narrative: Sustainable Mechanism for Improving Livelihoods & Household Empowerment (SMILE)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The aim of SMILE is to improve the wellbeing of OVCs in PEPFAR priority states by enabling them to fully access and utilize comprehensive and coordinated services. SMILE will integrate TB services into its existing mandate in two states (Benue and Nassarawa) by screening vulnerable children for TB, and linking them to designated diagnostic and treatment facilities. The project will develop and implement context specific communication strategies in the communities where they work to improve awareness of TB..

title.narrative: Feed the Future Nigeria Livelihoods Project (Formerly SHARE)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): ..Using a multi-sector approach, the Feed the Future Nigeria Livelihoods Project will help 42,000 very poor households to grow their agriculture products, increase incomes, and improve nutrition. The project focuses on rural communities in Northern Nigeria (states of Sokoto and Kebbi), as well as the Federal Capital Territory. . .In FY 2016, activities will improve agricultural practices and promote a market-oriented approach to expand production. Vulnerable families will diversify their income and implement comprehensive nutrition activities in their communities. To help some of the most vulnerable families prosper, the project will distribute cash transfers to help meet nutritional needs, recover assets, and overcome barriers to income-generating activities. . .To support sustainability, the project will strengthen the institutional capacity of government systems to implement poverty reduction programs and reinforce accountability between the government and citizens..

(Nigeria): .The goal of the Family Health Plus (FH+) project is to strengthen proficiency of public sector health providers to deliver high-quality family planning (FP) services and to empower users to demand quality FP. The project improves access to voluntary long-acting FP in 20 states in Nigeria through the implementation of high-impact approaches at the national and subnational levels. . .With FY 2016 funds, FH+ will scale-up activities to train both mid- and low-cadre staff members within the context of Nigeria's national policy on health task shifting and task sharing. The training will focus on the delivery of long-acting, reversible contraceptives (LARCs), as well as post-partum family planning methods. This will increase the pool of proficient FP service providers across more public health facilities extending to rural, hard to reach communities at the sub-national level. It will also complement capacity building efforts with community mobilization and outreach activities..

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The activity supports the long-term stability of Nigeria's electoral institutions. The activity provides demand-driven assistance to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and other election management bodies to strengthen their professionalism and capacity, leading to greater public confidence in election outcomes. Initiatives will train permanent INEC staff for off-cycle gubernatorial elections and continue the implementation of its strategic plan for the 2019 general elections. The activity will provide technical assistance to INEC to: improve voter register accuracy; develop more effective electoral dispute resolution mechanisms; improve new technology such as biometric card readers; strengthen internal efficiency and knowledge management; and provide voter education outreach to marginalized populations.

title.narrative: The Electoral Empowerment of Civil Society Project

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The Electoral Empowerment of Civil Society Project (EECSP) builds the capacity of civil society organizations (CSOs) to conduct domestic election monitoring and voter education. ..FY 2018 funds will support the recruitment and training of domestic monitors for the 2019 general elections and off-cycle gubernatorial elections, and strengthen the organizational capacity of CSOs, with special attention to financial management. FY 2018 funds will also increase the participation by marginalized groups (women, youth, persons with disabilities, and internally displaced persons) in Nigerian political processes. Through these interventions, USAID anticipates that the technical, organizational, and political support provided to Nigeria's electoral system will produce credible outcomes and long-term sustainability of election institutions. ..Credible electoral and political processes contribute to strengthening good governance in Nigeria, which is one of the key priorities of the Integrated Country Strategy for Nigeria..

title.narrative: Local Partners Initiative on Orphans and Vulnerable Children (LOPIN-OVC)

description.narrative: The LOPIN 1 Project is a 5 years (August 2014 to August 2019) USAID funded project aimed at mitigating the impact of HIV/AIDS and other forms of vulnerability on children and their households. LOPIN is an accelerated and sustainable approach to mitigate the impact of HIV/AIDS on children and caregivers. It is designed to model inclusiveness in programming for Orphans and Vulnerable Children in selected states in the country in accordance with the National Priority Agenda. A critical component of the project is at the community level, where CBOs and CPCs have key roles in identifying and enrolling OVCs and vulnerable households and linking OVCs to services in health, education, nutrition and psychosocial support services. CBOs, with the support of the LGAs are also expected to guide the communities in Household economic empowering activities and to provide oversight for other activities in the communities, reporting accordingly to the LGA Social Welfare Officer, who in turn report to the State Desk officers in the State Ministries of Women Affairs. CBOs will be provided grants to conduct these critical interventions. Another innovation of the project is the secondment of ARFH LOPIN staff (State Programme Coordinators and State M&E Officers) to the State Ministry of Women Affairs to provide coaching, mentorship and hand holding in service provision as well as in the collection, validation of data. The project will also focus on strengthening stakeholders capacity to provide services as well as Public Private Partnership involvement.

title.narrative: Local Partners Initiative on Orphans and Vulnerable Children (LOPIN-OVC)

description.narrative: Widows and Orphans Empowerment Organization (WEWE) was authorized by United States Agency for International Development (USAID) Nigeria to implement the Local Partners Initiative for Orphans and Vulnerable Children (OVC) [LOPIN] in Region 2 which included Anambra and Imo State, the agreement was scaled up to two more states Akwa-Ibom and Rivers States. LOPIN 2 Project aimed at mitigating the impact of HIV/AIDS and other forms of vulnerability on children and their households. It is designed to model inclusiveness in programming for Orphans and Vulnerable Children in Nigeria in accordance with the National Priority Agenda. The project goal is to improve the quality of life of at least 340,000 VC from 68,000 households in Awka Ibom, Anambra, Imo, and Rivers State within 5 years. WEWE - LOPIN 2 proposes Nine (9) strategic approaches which are: (i) OVC Service Delivery, (ii) Quality Improvement Science, (iii) System Strengthening, (iv) Public - Public Partnerships (PPP), (v) HIV Prevention (vi) Gender Consideration, (vii) Operational Research, (ix) Linkages to Treatment, Care and Support.

title.narrative: Local Partners Initiative on Orphans and Vulnerable Children (LOPIN-OVC)

description.narrative: Local Partners for Orphan and Vulnerable Children (OVC) in Nigeria (LOPIN) Region 3 is a five-year, United State Agency for International Development (USAID)-funded project aimed at mitigating the impact of HIV/AIDS on children, households and families in Cross River and Ebonyi States. The project is focused on community-based, result-oriented and family focused interventions to increase capacity of local organizations and communities to positively respond to the needs of OVCs. LOPIN-3 is implemented by Health Initiatives for Safety and Stability in Africa (HIFASS) as the lead partner among other local consortium members which include People-To-People Health Foundation Nigeria (PPHFN), Calabar Arch-Diocesan Action Committee on AIDS (CAACA) and Catholic Diocese of Abakaliki, Succour and Development Services Initiatives (SUCCDEV). The Project has two strategic objectives: (i) To improve systems and structures at state, LGAs and communities to ensure provision of quality care, protection and support services to OVC and their households. (ii) To support improved organizational and technical capacities of local NGOs and CBOs to provide OVC care and support services in the two states.

title.narrative: Nigeria Education Data Survey Project (NEDS II) (2013-2014)

description.narrative: The NEDS 2010+ task order was designed to support the Nigeria Federal Ministry of Education (FMOE) in developing additional analyses of Nigeria Education Data Survey (NEDS) data and related activities involving mapping of the education sector and strengthening of the National Education Management Information Systems (NEMIS). As a complement to the 2010 NEDS, these analyses provided education stakeholders and decision makers in Nigeria with accurate and timely data for education policy and program planning. NEDS 2010+ consisted of three separate components: analysis of the NEDS 2010, an education sector mapping study, and capacity support to the FMOE's NEMIS unit.

The Nigeria Reading and Access Research Activity (RARA) is designed to carry out research in the areas of early grade reading and access to education in Nigeria. The project will identify factors that improve reading skills and increase access to schooling for out-of-school children, especially for girls and almajiri (Islamic boarding school children). RARA will also help inform government actors, donor partners, civil society, the private sector, and USAID technical staff in developing a more nuanced understanding of activities that can be taken to scale in northern Nigeria to achieve this goal.
