description.narrative: The project supports improved productivity, value-added processing and commercialized agriculture with the aim of increasing sales and jobs for agriculture-related businesses. It provides technical assistance and training to small agricultural producers and agribusinesses to improve productivity, facilitate credit and link producers to guaranteed markets.

title.narrative: Maximizing Agricultural Revenue and Key Enterprises in Targeted Sectors (MARKETS) II

description.narrative: (Nigeria): ..MARKETS II improves the incomes and nutrition of poor smallholder farmers through proven private sector demand driven interventions. The project focuses on farmers with five hectares or less of land and small-scale agricultural support services along targeted value chains. . .FY 2016, MARKETS II will support 200,000 farmers to access finance to purchase agro-inputs and expand production and sales, establish over 100 technology demonstration plots and train farmers in three states. It will also collaborate with Partnership Initiatives in the Niger Delta (PIND), an initiative with Chevron to link 1,000 out-growers to industrial processors. The project will also train 15,000 farmers on business skills and nutrition.. .A total of some 193,000 farmers are expected to apply new technologies and management practices on approximately 229,000 hectares of land. The value of new private sector investments is expected to reach $5.5 million. .

title.narrative: Strengthening Advocacy and Civic Engagement Project (SACE)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The Strengthening Advocacy and Civic Engagement (SACE) activity builds the civil society organizations (CSO) capacity to influence key democratic reforms. SACE supports CSOs advocating for improved service delivery in key social sectors such as health, education, and agriculture, while also promoting the rights of women, youth, and persons with disabilities. The activity utilizes local leadership and innovation in its approach to increase citizen participation in democratic processes and promote transparency and accountability in governance. It will mentor 17 issue-based CSO clusters (groupings of CSOs with similar advocacy goals) in advocacy, monitoring, and evaluation. Partners' increased capacity and improved advocacy skills are expected to result in better governance, more inclusive economic growth, and improved policies, especially for vulnerable populations.

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The Northern Education Initiative Plus (NEI+) activity addresses low literacy rates and mitigates causes of conflict in Northern Nigeria by assisting Bauchi and Sokoto states to increase access to basic education, especially for girls and Out-of-School-Children (OOSC). It aims to significantly improve reading outcomes for more than 1.4 million school-aged children. Activities include training teachers and learning facilitators in formal schools and non-formal learning centers, strengthening school-based management committees and civil society organizations, and persuading parents to enroll their children in local schools; and providing textbooks and learning materials. By working with four state Colleges of Education to include early grade reading concepts, techniques, practices, and materials in their curriculum, the activity will continue to build state capacity to deliver effective reading instruction. This will improve reading proficiency for 900,000 school-aged children in grades 1 to 3, and 500,000 out of school children in non-formal learning settings. In its final years of implementation, NEI+ will emphasize mainstreaming successful graduates, ages 6-11, into their local primary schools... ...

(Nigeria): USAID, General Electric, the Federal Ministry of Health, and select State Ministries of Health will improve the quality of maternal and newborn health care in priority states. Healthymagination will provide V-scan Access technology, a miniature ultra sound device, to health facilities in seven states. The device, coupled with relevant clinical training, will aid in the diagnosis of at-risk pregnancy and will assist health workers to monitor maternal and fetal health from the early indication of a pregnancy through birth. Ultrasound technology is already used in Nigeria, however, underserved communities that rely on the public sector have no access to clinicians who are adequately trained and have up-to-date technology. There is no evidence that ultrasounds are used for the purpose of sex selection or detection of genetic anomalies in Nigeria. With FY 2016 funding, USAID will support the roll-out, use, and monitoring of the technology to selected states in Nigeria...

title.narrative: Nigeria Center for Reading and Research and Development Activity (NCRRD)

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The Nigerian Center for Reading Research and Development (NCRRD) activity is a partnership between Florida State University (FSU) and Bayero University in Kano State (BUK). The cooperation between these universities seeks to achieve the following objectives: 1) familiarize and train BUK faculty on content and best practices in early grade reading instruction to enable the delivery of courses to pre-service teachers of primary grade reading; 2) engage six key BUK faculty in a series of one-semester scholarly residencies at FSU's Florida Center for Reading Research to familiarize them with the latest research in primary grade reading, to introduce them to the design, organization and objectives of a reading research center; and to study different models of academic program development, curricular content, and program design in reading; 3) engage key FSU faculty in advising BUK on the design and scope of the NCRRD; 4) support the infrastructural development of NCRRD, including computers and software; 5) engage key BUK and FSU faculty in collaborative research on primary grade reading in the Nigerian context; and 6) assist BUK in the development of a one-year postgraduate diploma and a master's degree program in the teaching of primary grade reading. This complements the reading instruction content for teacher training colleges that FSU is developing under a separate award, the Northern Education Initiative Plus activity.

title.narrative: Feed the Future Nigeria Agricultural Policy Project

description.narrative: (Nigeria): ..The Feed the Future Nigeria Agricultural Policy Activity aims to promote inclusive agricultural, productivity growth, improved nutritional outcomes, and enhanced livelihood resilience in Nigeria through an improved policy enabling environment. The project will achieve its goal through three principal activities: 1) conduct evidence-based policy analysis; 2) strengthen the capacity (through training) of government stakeholders at federal and state levels; and 3) promote policy dialogue among stakeholders in the agricultural sector. Through these three components, the Agricultural Policy Activity aims to improve policy processes driven by empirical evidence and based on active stakeholder dialogue. By supporting an enabling environment that helps Nigerian farmers become more self-reliant, the Agricultural Policy Activity will contribute to putting Nigeria on a firm path to self-reliance... .

A cross-sectoral conflict assessment focusing on USAID programs and the risk of violence during the 2015 presidential elections. The Mission sought guidance on how to implement programs in a conflict sensitive manner, emphasizing Do No Harm principles, and maximize peacebuilding opportunities. Given that USAID conducted a conflict assessment in Nigeria in 2010 and a desk study of violent extremism in 2013, the 2014 assessment focused primarily on how conflict dynamics have shifted since the 2011 elections in the areas where USAID is operating and how programs interact with those changing conflict dynamics.

description.narrative: (Nigeria): The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Activity provides cross-sectoral, Mission-wide support on project and activity level monitoring, evaluation, and learning. The goal of this activity is to help transform USAID/Nigeria into a premier practitioner of program monitoring and evaluation rooted in organizational learning and adaptation. The MEL Activity provides continuous, on-the-ground, on-demand and systematic support to all USAID/Nigeria technical teams, sectors, and implementing partners on performance monitoring, data verification, performance and impact evaluations, project- and activity-level monitoring, evaluation and learning plans, organizational learning, capacity building and knowledge management. ..Due to security restrictions for USAID/Nigeria staff, the MEL Activity supports third-party, field-based monitoring to augment the Mission's activity monitoring efforts. The MEL Activity is also designed to support enhanced accountability and engagement with non-USAID stakeholders so that USAID can benefit from their perspectives through shared learning and problem solving that improves Mission results and achievement..

USAID has awarded DIG a contract to implement the two-year Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene Coordination Project (WCP) in Bauchi and Kaduna States of Nigeria, funded under the Making Cities Work contracting mechanism. The primary objective of this project is to achieve the dual benefits of improved health and well-being for Nigerians through increased and more financially-sustainable access to water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) services and to build the confidence of the public in its governments ability to deliver basic services. Improving governance is fundamental to improving WASH service delivery. Therefore, DIG is working directly with civil society organizations, non-governmental organizations, water boards, and state governments, helping to ensure transparent and accountable governance as well as the inclusive and equitable delivery of WASH services. The project expects to build on progress already achieved in the WASH sector in Nigeria, expanding USAIDs strategic role and accelerating reforms specifically in Bauchi and Kaduna States.

title.narrative: Support for Strategic Information and Project Management Services (S4SIPMS)

description.narrative: Support for Strategic Information and Program Management Services (S4SIPMS) Project will support of the United States Agency for International Development (USAID)/Nigeria Office of HIV/AIDS and Tuberculosis (TB) in meeting its strategic information and program management needs as required by the Office of Global AIDS Coordinator (OGAC) and USAID. In order for USAID/Nigeria to accomplish its goal in the fight against HIV/AIDS, the Mission was tasked with supporting the strengthening of the Nigerian national health system through the use of Site Improvement through Monitoring Systems (SIMS). SIMS continuously monitors and assesses sites receiving PEPFAR funding to ensure that program implementation is effective and of high quality, and that the sites adhere to national and international standards. The Project will achieve these goals achievement of the objectives below: Planning and Conducting SIMS Assessments; Capacity Building for Data Use; and Synthesize Evaluation Lessons and Analyze to determine Policy Implications.

description.narrative: Nigeria Northern Education Initiative (NEI)

To provide a more complete picture of schooling needs at the local level, RTI oversaw the third and largest Nigeria Education Data Survey (NEDS), covering approximately 30,000 households with school-aged children spread across all 36 states of Nigeria and the capital Abuja. Technical Assistance to implement the 2009 Nigeria Education Data Survey (NEDS), aimed at updating records from the previous survey done in 2004, the result of which, it is anticipated, will help basic education administrators, policy and decision makers and other stakeholders to make quality policies and take better decision that will positively affect basic education in Nigeria.

title.narrative: Community-Based Orphans and Vulnerable Children (CUBS) project

description.narrative: The Community-Based Orphans and Vulnerable Children (CUBS) project in Nigeria provides support and coordination for scaling up of HIV activities using community-based responses to identify, locate and protect orphans and vulnerable children (OVC). Under the AIDSTAR indefinite quantity contract (IQC) mechanism, Management Sciences for Health (MSH), is joined by Africare in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Women Affairs and Social Development and the State Ministries of Women Affairs to address these focus areas under a five-year contract. Through the CUBS project, PEPFAR strengthens the capacity of federal and state government agencies to plan and implement OVC programs. The project will support the implementation of Nigerias National Plan of Action on OVC by developing and strengthening community based service delivery for orphans and vulnerable children.

Through DIV, USAID seeks to identify and rigorously test promising projects with the potential to significantly (rather than incrementally) improve development outcomes, and help replicate and scale projects that are proven successful. USAID/DIV expects its most successful investments will have an accelerated growth path to reach millions of beneficiaries worldwide within 10 years.
